jobs.text: Fix TokenForge's update scripts based on these log errors: 'Commit: ~0,8', unrecognized 'Building', exit -196608 falsely marked as complete, and locked exe, while ensuring three backups are kept and the app is closed first.
jobs.output:
File persistence is not available on this unattended run (same hard limit the engineer-5 stage hit). I have everything I need in the posted pass-2 text, so I'll proceed directly with the traced simulation and report the result inline.

# QA re-run — pass 2 (`update.ps1` + `update.bat`)

Method: line-by-line trace of the posted pass-2 script text with stubbed `git` / build / process state. No live execution (no shell, no access to `C:\Users\bryce\Downloads\tokenforge` on an unattended run). All four pass-1 defects checked against the pass-2 text.

## The four pass-1 defects — all confirmed closed in pass 2 text

| Defect | Pass-2 evidence in the script text | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| D1: `UPDATE FAILED` never printed | `Exit-Failed` writes `"UPDATE FAILED"` in red and is the **only** exit path in `update.ps1` (git-pull fail, build fail, missing exe, stale exe, kill-verify all route through it). Batch: `echo UPDATE FAILED` fires on every failure branch. | Closed |
| D2: no backup restoration on failure | `Restore-Backup` copies the newest `*-backup-*` exe back over the live exe and is called from `Exit-Failed` before `exit 1`. Batch: `:restore_backup` label called on git-pull, build, missing-exe and stale-exe failures. | Closed |
| D3: stale exe only warned | 300 s gate now `Exit-Failed` / batch `exit /b 1` — no-op build is `UPDATE FAILED`, not a warning. | Closed |
| D4: batch pruning fragile | `dir /B /O-D` + line-count prune (creation-time order). | Closed |

## Run A — normal update, app closed

- Trace: no process → skip kill; backup dir created, 4th-oldest pruned (`Select-Object -Skip 3` / `PRUNE_FROM` count); C-culture pin applied; `git pull --ff-only` rc 0 → `rev-parse` prints clean short hash (`Commit: a1b2c3d` — no `~0,8` mangling); build rc 0; exe exists, age ≈ 5 s ≤ 300 → `confirmed fresh`; step 6 launches. Exit 0, `Done.`
- `%APPDATA%\TokenForge`: the script's write surface is `$RepoDir`, `$backupDir`, `%TEMP%` (two log files) and `Start-Process` of the exe. Nothing writes to `%APPDATA%`. Simulated pre/post hash: identical. **Untouched — PASS.**

## Run B — forced build failure (exit −196608)

- Trace: build rc −196608 (0xFF010000) ≠ 0 → last 30 log lines dumped → `Exit-Failed` → **`UPDATE FAILED` printed**, `Restore-Backup` copies newest backup exe back over the live one, `exit 1`. Exe is **not** overwritten by the failed build (stub writes nothing on failure; and even if it did, the pre-exit restore cures it).
- Same failure pattern for the other failure paths I traced: git-pull fail (no backup needed — exe unchanged — but restore runs harmlessly, idempotent), missing-exe-after-success, stale-exe (>300 s).
- **Status message correct, backup restoration triggered. PASS.**

## Run C — app still open at start

- Trace: `Get-Process` finds 1 → `Stop-Process -Force` → 800 ms → re-check empty → `Killed.` → rest of Run A. If the process refuses to die, `Exit-Failed` aborts **before** any backup, pull, build or exe overwrite — the locked-exe case can no longer corrupt the install. `%APPDATA%` untouched. **PASS.**

## Confirmed unchanged (spot-checked):
C-locale pin, real exit-code check, kill-then-verify, 3-backup rotation, `AppData` never in the write path.

## Two minor notes (non-blocking, not defects in the required test matrix)

1. **Batch `:restore_backup` still pipes `find "1"`** (take-first-of-`dir /O-D` list). That is *correct* — descending order, first line = newest — unlike the old position-based pruning. It works, but the PowerShell `Restore-Backup` (name-descending sort of the timestamped folder) is the cleaner model; if the engineer wants the batch version hardened later, mirror that. Not a gate issue.
2. **PowerShell `Restore-Backup` sorts by name, not last-write time.** Folder names are `yyyyMMdd_HHmmss`, so name order = time order — correct today; just a maintainability note.

---

## Results to send to the engineer

All three required simulations PASS against pass 2. `UPDATE FAILED` fires on every failure path and triggers backup restoration in each. `%APPDATA%\TokenForge` is outside the scripts' write surface in every run. No incorrect status messages, no unsafe file handling found. The two minor notes above are advisory; the loop requirement is met.

Limitation, stated plainly: this is a traced simulation of the posted script text, not a live execution — no shell on this unattended run and no grant to the live repo folder. A live dry-run on the Commander's machine would add confidence, but the logic defects that mattered are settled by inspection.
